newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro shares mixed, dollar up ahead of US data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro shares mixed, dollar up ahead of US data.

text.p: European shares were mixed in morning trading on Wednesday, showing little reaction to an overnight fall on Wall Street but with worries over higher interest rates very much on investors' minds.
The Frankfurt and Paris bourses traded higher but interest rate fears sent London, Europe's busiest stock market, lower after fluctuating up and down.
On the currency market, the dollar progressed against the mark and the yen and the pound recovered some of its poise after slipping on pre-election jitters.

Markets generally were focusing on key U.S. February consumer price data due at 1330 GMT for clues on likely action at next week's meeting of the policy-making committee of the U.S. central bank, the Federal Reserve.
Concern about higher American interest rates to keep a lid on inflation had depressed U.S. shares on Tuesday. Traders noted a growing belief in world markets that U.S. rates will rise on March 25.
"Inflation data in the U.S. has been consistently benign," one London share dealer said. "But that won't stop the Fed raising rates pre-emptively because the economy is very strong."
U.S. shares were mostly lower again in European business ahead of Wall Street's reopening on Wednesday.
British shares had opened lower after news that Wall Street ended almost 59 points or 0.85 percent weaker -- more than double the 25-point loss it showed as London closed for business on Tuesday.

They then moved ahead, aided by firmer bonds and a strong performance by British Telecom (up 18 pence at 460), before slipping as stronger-than-expected data revived the spectre of higher British interest rates after the general election on May 1.
"We were doing well until the figures. Now everyone is talking about inflation and an interest rate rise after the election," one dealer said.

British January average earnings rose five percent year-on-year, versus forecasts of 4.25 percent, and retail sales climbed 0.5 percent in February and 4.4 percent year-on-year, against a predicted 0.1 and 3.6 percent.
German shares, however, advanced after February money supply data and a key business confidence survey were viewed as mildly positive signs for the economy.

M3 money growth slowed to a 9.1 percent annualised rate from the fourth 1996 quarter from January's 11.7 percent rise. The Ifo institute February German business climate index rose to 93.6 from 93.3 in January.
Steel giants Thyssen and Krupp have agreed to talk on setting up a joint steel company but their shares were still suspended after news of Krupp's hostile takeover bid.

After a two-day downward correction, French shares held on to modest gains at midsession, aided by a stronger dollar, good news for exporters, and steady bonds -- but with investors sidelined ahead of the U.S. data.
"Paris has in the past few days fallen much more than Wall Street," one dealer said as the Paris bourse shrugged off the New York market's overnight decline.
The dollar, meanwhile, moved above 1.68 marks and 123 yen in cautious trading ahead of further economic news from the other side of the Atlantic.

Another gainer was the pound, hit by jitters this week after confirmation of the election date but showing a revival following the British data, including a drop in the February jobless rate to 6.2 percent from January's 6.5.
Sterling strengthened to 2.6850 marks from 2.6607 overnight and to $1.5945 from $1.5887.
Gold also revived after a sharp sell off and subsequent rally emanating largely from New York.
News that the Russian central bank planned to buy 90 tonnes of gold this year for reserves was positive, dealers said. "Anything which keeps gold off the market is mildly bullish," one said.
CURRENCIES AT 1215 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.6840 marks and 123.20 yen, compared with Tuesday's late European levels of 1.6762 and 122.44.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1215 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 4.3 points at 4,352.5.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was 28.84 ahead at 3,320.03.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 11.43 points at 2,585.38.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was quoted around its morning fix of $348.95, up from the previous London close of $346.25. Silver rose to $5.18 from $5.10. Platinum was up around $3 at $377.25.
